Read an mzLib spectral library (.msl): one row per precursor, or per fragment ion

library_read.Rd

Read an mzLib spectral library (.msl) as one row per precursor, or with fragments one row per fragment ion, with mzLib's not-available sentinels as nulls.

Answers what is in this spectral library? For each precursor - a peptide or proteoform at one charge - the m/z, retention time and ion mobility a search expects to see it at, its labels and provenance, and on request the fragment ions it expects in the MS2 spectrum. MetaMorpheus and mzLib write libraries in mzLib's binary .msl format; this reads one with mzLib's own reader, MslFileTypeHandler.Open and MslLibrary.GetEntry.

Usage

library_read(path, fragments = FALSE, index_only_threshold = NULL, limit = NULL,
  offset = 0, out = NULL, timeout = NULL)

Arguments

path

Path to a .msl file. Any other extension is an mzlib_usage_error: text libraries (.msp) are not read here.

fragments

One row per fragment ion instead of one per precursor, with the precursor's columns repeated on each row. FALSE by default: a library has tens of fragments per precursor, so pair it with limit or out for a large one.

index_only_threshold

A library this many bytes or larger opens index-only; a smaller one loads whole. NULL (the default) sends nothing, so mzLib's own default applies: MslFileTypeHandler.DefaultIndexOnlyThresholdBytes, 1073741824 bytes (1 GiB) in the pinned build. 0 opens every library index-only. The rows are the same either way.

limit

Maximum precursors to return; with fragments each gives one row per fragment ion. NULL, the default, returns all of them.

offset

Precursors to skip, in precursor_index order.

out

Write a tab-separated table here and return only a summary. The path must end in .tsv (any case); any other is an mzlib_usage_error before a read. The file keeps the wire's 0-based precursor_index.

timeout

Seconds to allow, or NULL (the default) to wait.

Details

Rows come in the library's stored order (precursor_index), not by m/z: sort on precursor_mz for that. mzLib's "not available" values - an ion mobility of 0.0, a NaN q-value, an NCE of 0, an empty protein accession - arrive as NA.

Large libraries open index-only: precursors in memory, fragment blocks left on disk. mzLib decides by file size (1 GiB by default in the pinned build); pass index_only_threshold to move the line. The rows are the same either way.

Value

An mzlibr_library_records. record_count counts the precursors in the whole library, before offset and limit; returned_count the precursors returned (precursors, not rows: the unit limit and offset count in), 0 with out; row_count the rows of records, one per fragment ion with fragments; offset the precursors skipped; truncated whether precursors were left behind.

The library's facts: reader ("MslLibrary"); format_version, the file's .msl format version; is_compressed (a compressed library always loads whole) and is_index_only; target_count, precursors that are not decoys, entrapment targets included; decoy_count, decoy precursors, entrapment decoys included; proteoform_count, precursors whose molecule_type is "Proteoform"; and min_precursor_mz and max_precursor_mz, in m/z, NA when the library has no precursors. fragments_included says whether the rows are fragment ions, and index_only_threshold the threshold applied, in bytes: yours, or mzLib's default.

file_type is always NA (.msl is not one of mzLib's SupportedFileType members); rows_not_read is always NA: rows are not counted for a binary library, because mzLib checks the whole file before returning any precursor; retention_time_unit is NA at the top level, because the unit varies by precursor - it is a column. absent_fields names the columns this library has no source for, so every value is NA (ion_mobility when no precursor has one, protein_accession and protein_name without a protein table, gene_name without gene names); failed_fields the columns whose read threw on some rows; excluded_fields is always empty; caveats says what the table cannot be trusted to mean. output says where the table was written, or is NULL.

records is a data.frame, or NULL with out. One row per precursor: precursor_index (1-based in R, the position in the library and the row order), full_sequence (mzLib bracket notation), base_sequence, precursor_mz in m/z, charge_state (a charge), retention_time in iRT or minutes per row and retention_time_unit ("iRT" or "minutes"), ion_mobility in 1/K0 (V s/cm2; NA where mzLib stores 0.0), is_decoy, is_entrapment, decoy_contaminant_target ("T", "D", "ET" or "ED"), protein_accession, protein_name and gene_name (NA where mzLib stores an empty string), is_proteotypic, q_value (a fraction, 0 to 1; NA where mzLib stores NaN, a predicted library), elution_group_id, molecule_type, source_type ("Predicted", "Empirical" or "EmpiricalRefined"), dissociation_type and nce (an NCE, a whole number; NA where mzLib stores 0).

With fragments = TRUE, one row per fragment ion: those columns, then fragment_count (fragment ions of the precursor), fragment_mz in m/z, fragment_intensity (relative intensity within the precursor, 0 to 1), product_type, secondary_product_type and secondary_fragment_number (NA for a terminal ion), fragment_number, residue_position (NA for a custom-loss fragment, whose stored position mzLib reads back as 0), fragment_charge (a charge), neutral_loss in Da (0 is no loss), is_internal, is_diagnostic, exclude_from_quant and annotation. A precursor with no fragment ions is one row with those cells NA.

Three things to know before you use the numbers

Retention time has a unit per row. A library stores either an indexed retention time (iRT) or run minutes for each precursor (MslLibraryEntry.RtIsCalibrated), and one library can hold both. Read retention_time_unit on each row; there is no conversion between them without a calibration against a run.

**"Not available" is NA, not a number.** A text library converted to .msl (from .msp) has no NCE, dissociation type, q-value, ion mobility or protein, so those are NA (and dissociation_type is "Unknown").

The library is unfiltered. Decoys (D, ED) and entrapment precursors (ET, ED) are rows; filter on is_decoy or decoy_contaminant_target before counting targets.

Parameters: units, ranges and defaults

path

path; required; range .msl, any case (MslFileTypeHandler.IsMslFile). An mzLib binary spectral library. Any other extension is a usage error before the file is opened: text libraries (.msp) are not read by this verb.

fragments

flag; default FALSE. One row per fragment ion instead of one per precursor: the precursor's columns repeated on each row, then the fragment's. A precursor with no fragment ions gives one row whose fragment cells are null. Given with a value is a usage error.

index_only_threshold (wire --index-only-threshold)

int; in bytes; default 1073741824; range >= 0. Passed to MslFileTypeHandler.Open: a library this size or larger opens index-only (precursors in memory, fragment blocks read from disk on demand), a smaller one is loaded whole. Absent means mzLib's own default, MslFileTypeHandler.DefaultIndexOnlyThresholdBytes, 1073741824 bytes (1 GiB) at the pin; the bridge sends no value of its own. 0 opens every library index-only. The rows are the same in both modes; only memory and speed differ.

offset

int; in precursors; default 0; range >= 0. Skip this many precursors, in precursor_index order. A window, not a cursor: the library is opened again on every call.

limit

int; in precursors; default absent; range >= 0. Return at most this many precursors; with fragments each gives one row per fragment ion. Absent means no limit.

out

path; default absent; range .tsv only, any case (PYB-1). Write the table to this path as tab-separated text instead of returning columns. Must differ from path. Parent directories are created. Must end in .tsv, any case (PYB-1); any other extension, or none, is a usage error before the library is opened, and no extension is appended.

Returned fields

Each field with its type, its unit, and what NA means when it is NA.

path

string; never NA. Absolute path of the library.

file_type

string; NA when always: .msl is not an mzLib SupportedFileType (mzLib reads it with MslLibrary, outside FileReader), so there is no type name to give. The mzLib SupportedFileType, for parity with the reader verbs.

reader

string; never NA. Always MslLibrary, the mzLib class that read the file.

format_version

int; never NA. The file's .msl format version (MslFileHeader.FormatVersion): 1 to 3 at the pin, where 3 allows compression (MslFormat.CurrentVersion).

is_compressed

bool; never NA. The fragment section is zstd-compressed (MslLibrary.IsCompressed). A compressed library always loads whole.

is_index_only

bool; never NA. mzLib opened the library index-only (MslLibrary.IsIndexOnly): at or above index_only_threshold, and not compressed.

target_count

int; in precursors; never NA. Precursors that are not decoys, entrapment targets included (MslLibrary.TargetCount).

decoy_count

int; in precursors; never NA. Decoy precursors, entrapment decoys included (MslLibrary.DecoyCount).

proteoform_count

int; in precursors; never NA. Precursors whose molecule_type is Proteoform (MslLibrary.ProteoformCount).

min_precursor_mz

float; in m/z; NA when the library has no precursors. Smallest precursor m/z (MslLibrary.MinPrecursorMz).

max_precursor_mz

float; in m/z; NA when the library has no precursors. Largest precursor m/z (MslLibrary.MaxPrecursorMz).

record_count

int; in precursors; never NA. Precursors in the whole library, before the window (MslLibrary.PrecursorCount).

rows_not_read

int; in rows; NA when always: the file is binary and mzLib validates it whole (magic, version, footer, precursor count, CRC-32) before returning any entry, so every precursor is read or the call fails. Data rows that did not become records.

retention_time_unit

string; NA when always: the unit varies by precursor, so it is the retention_time_unit column. Always null for this verb.

caveats

string[]; never NA. What this table cannot be trusted to mean, each citing the mzLib source.

column_names

string[]; never NA. Column order.

absent_fields

string[]; never NA. Columns this library has no source for, from its file flags (MslFormat.FileFlag*): ion_mobility when no precursor has one, protein_accession and protein_name when there is no protein table, gene_name when there are no gene names. Null in every row (BULK.md section 4).

failed_fields

string[]; never NA. 'field: ExceptionType' for each column whose read threw on some returned rows; those cells are null.

excluded_fields

object[]; never NA. Always empty: every field crosses, the fragments with the fragments flag.

error

object; NA when always, for a single path: a library that cannot be read fails the call instead. {kind, type, message}; non-null only in a files[] entry under on-error skip.

fragments_included

bool; never NA. Whether the rows are fragment ions (the fragments flag).

index_only_threshold

int; in bytes; never NA. The threshold MslFileTypeHandler.Open applied: the one given, or mzLib's default, 1073741824 at the pin.

returned_count

int; in precursors; never NA. Precursors returned in columns (the unit offset and limit count in); 0 when written to out.

row_count

int; in rows; never NA. Rows in columns: returned_count without fragments, one per fragment ion (or one for a precursor with none) with them; 0 when written to out.

offset

int; in precursors; never NA. The offset applied.

truncated

bool; never NA. True whenever precursors were left out by offset or limit.

records (wire columns)

table; NA when the table was written to out instead. Column name to per-row values, in column_names order.

output

object; NA when out was not given. {path, format: "tsv", row_count} when out was given.

Columns of records

precursor_index

int; never NA. 0-based position of the precursor in the library (MslPrecursorIndexEntry.PrecursorIdx): the key MslLibrary.GetEntry takes, and the row order. Not m/z order.

full_sequence

string; never NA. Modified sequence in mzLib bracket notation, e.g. PEPTM[Common Variable:Oxidation on M]IDE (MslLibraryEntry.FullSequence).

base_sequence

string; never NA. The bare residues (MslLibraryEntry.BaseSequence).

precursor_mz

float; in m/z; never NA. Precursor m/z, (M + zH)/z (MslLibraryEntry.PrecursorMz), stored as a 32-bit float.

charge_state

int; in charge; never NA. Precursor charge (MslLibraryEntry.ChargeState).

retention_time

float; in iRT or min (per row); never NA. Indexed retention time, or a run-calibrated time in minutes, as retention_time_unit says (MslLibraryEntry.RetentionTime). iRT can be negative. 0 is passed through: mzLib documents no sentinel for it.

retention_time_unit

string; never NA. iRT or minutes, from MslLibraryEntry.RtIsCalibrated (false: iRT; true: run-specific minutes). Per row because one library can hold both.

ion_mobility

float; in 1/K0 (V s/cm2); NA when mzLib's 0.0, which MslLibraryEntry.IonMobility documents as not available; in absent_fields when no precursor has one. Ion mobility as 1/K0 (MslLibraryEntry.IonMobility).

is_decoy

bool; never NA. A decoy precursor, entrapment decoys included (MslLibraryEntry.IsDecoy).

is_entrapment

bool; never NA. An entrapment precursor, target or decoy (MslLibraryEntry.IsEntrapment, mzLib #1383). Independent of is_decoy.

decoy_contaminant_target

string; never NA. T, D, ET or ED, from DecoyContaminantTargetLabel.For(is_decoy, false, is_entrapment). The .msl format has no contaminant flag, so C never appears.

protein_accession

string; NA when mzLib's empty string: the precursor has no protein (MslLibraryEntry.ProteinAccession); in absent_fields when the library has no protein table. Accession of the source protein, as stored, e.g. P04637.

protein_name

string; NA when mzLib's empty string: no protein, or no name for it (MslLibraryEntry.ProteinName); in absent_fields when the library has no protein table. Protein name, as stored.

gene_name

string; NA when mzLib's empty string: no protein, or no gene for it (MslLibraryEntry.GeneName); in absent_fields when the library has no gene names. Gene symbol, as stored, e.g. TP53.

is_proteotypic

bool; never NA. Expected to give a uniquely detectable signal (MslLibraryEntry.IsProteotypic), as the library's writer set it.

q_value

float; in fraction (0 to 1); NA when mzLib's NaN: no q-value is available, as for a purely predicted library (MslLibraryEntry.QValue). The library's q-value for the precursor; lower is better.

elution_group_id

int; never NA. Shared by every precursor of one base sequence, so charge states and modified forms co-elute (MslLibraryEntry.ElutionGroupId); mzLib's writer assigns it.

molecule_type

string; never NA. MslFormat.MoleculeType name: Peptide, Proteoform, Oligonucleotide or Glycopeptide.

source_type

string; never NA. MslFormat.SourceType name (MslLibraryEntry.Source): Predicted, Empirical, or EmpiricalRefined (predicted intensities, measured retention time or ion mobility).

dissociation_type

string; never NA. mzLib DissociationType name, e.g. HCD; Unknown when the library does not say (MslLibraryEntry.DissociationType).

nce

int; in NCE; NA when mzLib's 0: unknown or not applicable (MslLibraryEntry.Nce). Normalized collision energy, a whole number: the format stores NCE x 10 and mzLib divides by 10 as an integer.

fragment_count

int; in fragment ions; never NA. Fragment ions the precursor has, counted from the ions mzLib read; 0 for a precursor with none, whose one row has every fragment cell null. Present only with __fragments.

fragment_mz

float; in m/z; NA when the precursor has no fragment ions (fragment_count 0). Fragment m/z (MslFragmentIon.Mz), a 32-bit float. Rows are in the stored order, which mzLib's writer sorts by m/z. Present only with __fragments.

fragment_intensity

float; in relative intensity (0 to 1); NA when the precursor has no fragment ions. Intensity relative to the precursor's most intense fragment, which mzLib's writer scales to 1 (MslFragmentIon.Intensity). Not comparable across precursors. Present only with __fragments.

product_type

string; NA when the precursor has no fragment ions. mzLib ProductType name, e.g. b, y, c, zDot; for an internal ion, its N-terminal type (MslFragmentIon.ProductType). Present only with __fragments.

secondary_product_type

string; NA when a terminal ion (MslFragmentIon.SecondaryProductType is null for every terminal ion), or no fragment ions. An internal ion's C-terminal ProductType, e.g. y for bIy. Present only with __fragments.

fragment_number

int; NA when the precursor has no fragment ions. The ion's number in its series, e.g. 5 for b5; for an internal ion, its 0-based start residue (MslFragmentIon.FragmentNumber). Present only with __fragments.

secondary_fragment_number

int; NA when a terminal ion, for which mzLib stores 0 (MslFragmentIon.SecondaryFragmentNumber), or no fragment ions. An internal ion's end residue, exclusive. Present only with __fragments.

residue_position

int; NA when mzLib's 0: always for a fragment with a custom neutral loss, whose stored position the format reuses to index its loss table (MslReader.ConvertFragment); or no fragment ions. Residue position the ion was annotated from, as stored (MslFragmentIon.ResiduePosition): for a library mzLib built from its own products, the Product.ResiduePosition convention, fragment_number for N-terminal ions and length - fragment_number + 1 for C-terminal ones (mzLib #1408). Present only with __fragments.

fragment_charge

int; in charge; NA when the precursor has no fragment ions. Fragment charge (MslFragmentIon.Charge). Present only with __fragments.

neutral_loss

float; in Da; NA when the precursor has no fragment ions. Neutral-loss mass, negative for a loss (MslFragmentIon.NeutralLoss). 0 means no loss, and crosses as 0, not null: it is the value of the shift, not a missing one. Present only with __fragments.

is_internal

bool; NA when the precursor has no fragment ions. An internal ion (MslFragmentIon.IsInternalFragment). Present only with __fragments.

is_diagnostic

bool; NA when the precursor has no fragment ions. A diagnostic ion, ProductType D (MslFragmentIon.IsDiagnosticIon). Present only with __fragments.

exclude_from_quant

bool; NA when the precursor has no fragment ions. Marked to be left out of quantification, like DIA-NN's ExcludeFromAssay (MslFragmentIon.ExcludeFromQuant). Present only with __fragments.

annotation

string; NA when the precursor has no fragment ions. mzLib's library rendering (MslFragmentIon.Annotation), e.g. b5, y3-18.0106, bIy[2-5] or y4^2+: the loss signed to four decimals and the charge appended, unlike Product.Annotation. Present only with __fragments.

Errors

Each is an R condition carrying the class shown and mzlib_error; see mzlib_error. A condition that mentions paths-stdin, threads or on-error comes only from library_read_many().

mzlib_usage_error (usage)

path missing or blank; the file does not exist, or is a directory; its extension is not .msl (MslFileTypeHandler.IsMslFile)

mzlib_usage_error (usage)

fragments given a value; index-only-threshold, offset, limit or out given with no value; index-only-threshold not a whole number, or below 0; offset or limit below 0 or not an integer; out resolving to the same file as path

mzlib_usage_error (usage)

out (with path or paths-stdin) whose extension is not .tsv, any case, including none (PYB-1); checked before any input is opened

mzlib_bridge_error (correctness)

mzLib cannot read the library: FormatException for a bad magic number, version, footer or precursor count, InvalidDataException for a CRC-32 mismatch (MslReader); the error type is mzLib's exception name

mzlib_usage_error (usage)

paths-stdin with path, offset or limit; paths-stdin with a value; no paths on stdin; a repeated path; threads 0 or below -1; on-error not fail or skip; on-error skip with a single path; out naming an input

mzlib_usage_error (usage)

with on-error fail, an input that is missing or not a .msl: the usage error of that input, prefixed 'Input <i> (<path>)'

mzlib_bridge_error (correctness)

with on-error fail, mzLib failing to read an input: that input's own error type, message prefixed 'Input <i> (<path>)'

mzlib_usage_error (usage)

the answer is too large to return as one JSON document (PYB-3 part 1). Message: 'this read (N records) is too large to return as one document; use --limit/--offset or --out'. A library with fragments is the likeliest case: write it to out.

mzlib_service_unavailable (service_unavailable)

Never raised by this verb.

Caveats

  • Rows are in the library's stored order, by precursor_index, not by m/z: mzLib's own MslLibrary.GetAllEntries enumerates in ascending precursor m/z instead. Sort on precursor_mz for that order.

  • retention_time is iRT for some precursors and run minutes for others: read retention_time_unit on each row (MslLibraryEntry.RtIsCalibrated). A library can hold both, so never plot or compare the column without it. There is no conversion: iRT becomes minutes only through a calibration against a run.

  • The library is unfiltered: decoys (D, ED) and entrapment precursors (ET, ED) are rows. Filter on is_decoy, or on decoy_contaminant_target, before counting targets.

  • A retention_time of 0 may mean the source had none: MslLibraryEntry.FromLibrarySpectrum, the path mzLib converts a text library through, writes RetentionTime ?? 0.0, and mzLib documents no sentinel for it, so 0 is passed through as a value.

  • nce is a whole number: the format stores NCE x 10 and MslReader reads it back with integer division, so an NCE of 27.5 reads as 27.

  • A library converted from a text library (.msp) has no NCE, dissociation type, q-value, ion mobility or protein: LibrarySpectrum has no field for them, and MslLibraryEntry.FromLibrarySpectrum fills mzLib's not-available defaults, so nce and q_value are null and dissociation_type is Unknown.

  • precursor_mz, retention_time and ion_mobility are stored as 32-bit floats and widened to double by mzLib, so 465.74 reads back as 465.739990234375. The extra digits are the float, not a measurement; round them for display.

  • offset and limit count PRECURSORS. With fragments, each precursor gives one row per fragment ion.

  • With fragments: residue_position is null for every fragment with a custom neutral loss, because the .msl format reuses that field to index its loss table and MslReader reads it back as 0.

  • With fragments: fragment_intensity is relative within its precursor, 0 to 1, because mzLib's writer scales each precursor's most intense fragment to 1 (MslWriter). It is not comparable across precursors.

  • Index-only (at or above index_only_threshold) keeps memory to the precursors, but with fragments every fragment block is read twice from disk: once to count the rows, once to write them. mzLib keeps each precursor's stored fragment count private, so the bridge cannot size the table without reading them.

Performance

Every call starts one bridge process, which costs a .NET start-up before any work. For many files call library_read_many() once rather than looping this function: one process, one start-up, and the thread count stated on the wire.

Same verb in other bindings

  • Python (pyMzLib): pymzlib.library.read; many files: pymzlib.library.read_many

  • Rust (mzLibRust): mzlib::library::read_with with LibraryReadOptions; many files: mzlib::library::read_many

  • R (mzLibR): library_read; many files: library_read_many

Since

Wire protocol 1; pyMzLib 0.6.0; mzLibRust not yet shipped; mzLibR not yet shipped.

Not yet verified

The spec records these as open. They are listed rather than hidden:

  • Text libraries (.msp, pDeep, ms2pip) could be read through the same table: mzLib's MslConverter.FromMspFile parses one into an in-memory MslLibrary. Left out of v1 because the conversion fills not-available defaults for every field LibrarySpectrum lacks, and because SpectralLibrary picks the text dialect from the file name. Revisit on demand.

  • fragment_count is carried only with fragments: without them mzLib's index-only entries have an empty fragment list (MslLibrary.GetEntry(i, false), 'do not rely on MatchedFragmentIons being empty or full'), and the stored MslPrecursorRecord.FragmentCount is not public. A public count would give the precursor table this column at no I/O cost (PUSH-TO-MAINLAND).

  • No decoy filter is offered: MslLibrary.GetAllEntries(includeDecoys: false) has one, but GetAllEntries yields m/z order with no index, so the bridge reads by index and the caller filters on is_decoy. A GetAllEntries overload with includeFragments, or one that yields the index, would let the bridge wrap it directly.

See also

library_read_many, readers_read_spectra for the runs a library is searched against

Examples


lib <- library_read("synthetic_library.msl")
lib
#> <mzlibr_library_records> E:\CodeReview\wt-py-library-read\pkg\python\tests\fixtures\library\synthetic_library.msl: 6 precursors (4 target, 2 decoy), .msl format 3
#>   precursor m/z 406.242 to 952.493
#>   6 precursor(s) returned
#>   ! retention_time is in iRT and minutes: read retention_time_unit on each row
lib$records[, c("precursor_index", "full_sequence", "decoy_contaminant_target",
                "retention_time", "retention_time_unit")]
#>   precursor_index     full_sequence decoy_contaminant_target retention_time
#> 1               1          PEPTIDEK                        T           35.2
#> 2               2          KEDITPEP                        D           35.2
#> 3               3          PEPTLDEK                       ET           21.4
#> 4               4          KEDLTPEP                       ED           33.0
#> 5               5       ELVISLIVESK                        T           61.7
#> 6               6 MAHVRSGKHQIPAEALQ                        T           48.0
#>   retention_time_unit
#> 1                 iRT
#> 2                 iRT
#> 3             minutes
#> 4                 iRT
#> 5                 iRT
#> 6                 iRT
# A predicted precursor: mzLib's "not available" values are NA.
lib$records[5, c("ion_mobility", "q_value", "nce", "protein_accession")]
#>   ion_mobility q_value nce protein_accession
#> 5           NA      NA  NA              <NA>

# One precursor's fragment ions:
ions <- library_read("synthetic_library.msl", fragments = TRUE, limit = 1)
c(precursors = ions$returned_count, rows = ions$row_count)
#> precursors       rows 
#>          1          6 
ions$records[, c("annotation", "fragment_mz", "fragment_intensity", "neutral_loss")]
#>   annotation fragment_mz fragment_intensity neutral_loss
#> 1         y1    147.1128               0.40      0.00000
#> 2         b2    227.1026               0.30      0.00000
#> 3         y2    276.1554               1.00      0.00000
